title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 1 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman presenting for a routine follow-up of her chronic conditions. She has a long-standing history of type 1 diabetes mellitus managed with insulin. She reports stable glucose levels and denies any recent acute issues. She also reports persistent sensations in her lower extremities consistent with polyneuropathy. She notes that these sensations have been present for several years.

Medication List
Insulin (long-acting and rapid-acting)

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. She appears in no acute distress. Physical exam reveals diminished sensation to light touch in both feet. Strength is intact in the lower extremities. Skin is intact without signs of ulceration.

Assessment
1. Type 1 diabetes: Stable on current insulin regimen.
2. Polyneuropathy: The patient's peripheral neuropathy is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. We will monitor her glucose levels at the next visit. No changes to the management of her neuropathy at this time.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
May 14, 2026
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code each separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: Provider documentation of no link overrides the presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
